subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call?
rationale: The report accepts either behavior and the choice affects how sandbox capability denial is surfaced, so automation should not silently pick a stricter or looser boundary.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warning channel while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution.

options.title: Fail explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so callers must choose a host or elevated path that can provide a PTY.

options.title: Adopt the fork PR after review
options.body: Review the open fork PR only after deciding that warning-only behavior is the desired product outcome.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warning channel while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for exec PTY support and sandbox/host routing is Peter Steinberger's work on the relevant files.
